summary: Concord Point Light at Havre de Grace, built in 1827, was kept mostly by the O'Neill family until automation in 1920; its keeper's house is now a museum.

light.characteristic: disputed: fixed white, then fixed red from 1879, then fixed green from 1931 (LighthouseFriends); fixed red to flashing white in 1919 (Bulletin 1919; Commissioner FY1919 lists a change from fixed to flashing); fixed green, last equipment used (1975 nomination)

lens.where: museum in the keeper's house (taken down in 2023)
lens.note: Fifth-order Fresnel lens on loan from the Coast Guard, mounted 1983; a 300 mm beacon loaned by the Coast Guard replaced it in the lantern in 2023.

structures.note: USLHS: 30 ft from base to lantern centre; LighthouseFriends: thirty-foot tower. The 1975 nomination's typed height is hard to read in the scan. Focal plane 32 ft above base (nomination).
One-and-a-half-storey keeper's house, restored as a museum (LighthouseFriends, Friends website).

access.note: Owned by the City of Havre de Grace. Grounds open; keeper's house and tower open in season (Saturdays and Sundays, April to October, per LighthouseFriends). Call ahead for tours.

facts.agency: City of Havre de Grace (owner); U.S. Coast Guard until 1975

keepers.name: Esther O'Neill
keepers.note: Widow of John O'Neill, Jr.; kept the light for eighteen years and resigned in 1881 (LighthouseFriends). A woman keeper in her own right, with the title keeper in the USLHS roster.

keepers.name: Gabriel Evans
keepers.note: Son-in-law of Esther O'Neill; assisted her during part of her years in charge (LighthouseFriends). Not on the USLHS roster. The dates given are Esther O'Neill's span (1863-1881), used only as the outer bounds of an approximate line; the source gives no dates for Evans.

keepers.name: Henry E. O'Neill
keepers.note: Son of Esther O'Neill. Roster ends 1918; LighthouseFriends says he stayed in the keeper's house until his death in 1919. The 1918 Bulletin gives his age as 77 and his service as 40 years.

corrections.why: USLHS place record gives 30 ft from base to lantern centre and LighthouseFriends says thirty feet. The 1975 nomination's height is hard to read in the scan. The record's 11.0 m (36 ft) comes from an unnamed source that the sources here do not support. For human review.

The nomination records discontinuance as an active light on 17 November 1975, and USLHS gives year discontinued 1975. A 300 mm beacon was installed in 2023 (LighthouseFriends), but no source read says whether it shows a light now.
USLHS gives 40 ft height of light above water (12.2 m); the nomination gives a focal plane 32 ft above the base, which is a different reference. For human review.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination and LighthouseFriends both date the tower to 1827 (Donohoo built it between May and November 1827); the record's 1827 is right.
The 1891 change from sixth to fifth order is confirmed by the Light-House Board report (fiscal 1892); LighthouseFriends' 1869 sixth-order date is not contradicted by anything read here.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements left open in the text: the signal (fixed red, flashing white in 1919 per the Bulletin and the Commissioner's report, fixed green from 1931 per LighthouseFriends and the nomination); the electrical versus acetylene change (LighthouseFriends: electric November 1918; Bulletin 1919: oil to acetylene); the year Henry E. O'Neill's keepership ended (roster 1918; LighthouseFriends: death 1919); tower height (nomination hard to read; USLHS and LighthouseFriends 30 ft; record 11.0 m). The 1918 Bulletin's OCR is poor: the name H. E. O'Neill is matched by the Bulletin's index for 1918-1923 (p. 27: O'Neill, H.E., keeper Havre de Grace, purchases liberty bonds, 45); the quoted phrases were read from the OCR and the letter's wording is not quoted. Lens date: LighthouseFriends gives 1855 for a steamer's lens and 1869 for a sixth order; a Wikipedia article gives 1854 (not cited). Chronicling America: a search for Concord Point with O'Neill, Maryland, 1918-1920 found no pages; Midland Journal and Cecil Whig pages mentioning the Havre de Grace lighthouse (1919-1929) were listed but not read. The Maryland Historical Trust 1975 nomination form (Whittington) was not separately fetched; the NRHP PDF is the copy read. The Coast Guard light list (1900 era) entries were checked only for names, not characteristics. No wreck or rescue at this light found. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the story now states the 1879 fixed-red change and the electrical (LighthouseFriends, November 1918) versus oil-to-acetylene (Bulletin 1919) disagreement. The 1918 Bulletin item is OCR'd badly: the letter's wording is read from the OCR, and the headline and index entry (O'Neill, H.E., keeper Havre de Grace, purchases liberty bonds, p. 45) agree. The 1919 and FY1919 Havre de Grace entries and the FY1892 and FY1894 Light-House Board entries were confirmed on the scanned text. Gabriel Evans's dates are Esther O'Neill's span and are approximate outer bounds only.
